title: Safety and accuracy diverge across deployment conditions in clinical large language models
abstract: arXiv:2605.04039v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Clinical large language models (LLMs) are commonly scaled by increasing model size, context length, retrieval complexity, or inference-time compute, on the assumption that higher accuracy implies safer behavior. In medicine, where a few confident or evidence-contradicting errors can outweigh average performance, this assumption may be incomplete. We introduce Safety-Focused Evaluation of Scaling (SaFE-Scale) and instantiate it on RadSaFE-200, a 200-question text-based radiology multiple-choice benchmark with clinician-defined clean evidence, conflict evidence, and option-level labels for high-risk error, unsafe answer, and evidence contradiction. Thirty-four local LLMs were evaluated across six deployment conditions spanning closed-book, evidence-grounded, standard and agentic retrieval- augmented generation (RAG), and max-context prompting. Clean clinician-written evidence, used as an upper-bound, produced the strongest joint gain,

translated_title: 临床大语言模型在不同部署条件下的安全性与准确性出现背离
translated_abstract: 临床大语言模型（LLM）通常通过增大模型规模、上下文长度、检索复杂度或推理时计算量来进行扩展，其前提假设是更高的准确性意味着更安全的行为。在医学领域，由于少数自信或与证据相矛盾的错误可能超过平均性能的影响，这一假设可能并不完整。我们提出了面向安全的扩展评估方法SaFE-Scale，并在RadSaFE-200上加以实现——这是一个包含200道题的基于文本的放射学多项选择基准，具有临床医生定义的干净证据、冲突证据，以及针对高风险错误、不安全答案和证据矛盾的选项级标签。研究对34个本地部署的大语言模型在六种部署条件下进行了评估，涵盖闭卷测试、证据锚定、标准与智能体检索增强生成（RAG）以及最大上下文提示。结果显示，作为上限参照的临床医生撰写的干净证据产生了最强的联合增益……
tldr: 该论文提出SaFE-Scale安全评估框架和RadSaFE-200放射学基准，通过对34个大语言模型在六种部署条件下的评估，揭示了临床大语言模型的准确率提升并不等于安全行为，二者在不同部署条件下会出现背离。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SaFE-Scale, a safety-focused evaluation framework, and the RadSaFE-200 radiology benchmark, demonstrating across 34 LLMs and six deployment conditions that safety and accuracy diverge in clinical large language models—higher accuracy does not necessarily imply safer behavior.
